claim: Letterman writes that what was sent for was of much service when it arrived but could not reach the field in time to protect the wounded from the drenching rain which fell after the battle.

claim: The Patriot Daughters of Lancaster write that patients long accustomed to nicely cooked meals loathed the food prepared at the cook house, a coarse piece of salt meat and a large half-boiled potato for dinner.

source.edition: Hospital scenes after the battle of Gettysburg, July 1863, by the Patriot Daughters of Lancaster (Lancaster: Daily Inquirer Steam Job Print, 1864; title page read)

quote: they had been so long accustomed to our nicely cooked meals, that their stomachs loathed the food prepared at the cook house. Imagine if you can, with their severe wounds, and no appetite, how they must have felt when they received for their dinner, a coarse piece of salt meat and large half-boiled potato.

data.description: the cook house sent out a coarse piece of salt meat and a large half-boiled potato for dinner

scene.may_show: A cook house sending out a coarse piece of salt meat and a half-boiled potato for the patients' dinner.
